name: Former McDonald Steel (U.S. Steel McDonald Works)
formerUse: Steel mill (Carnegie Steel / U.S. Steel McDonald Works, later McDonald Steel Corp.)
owner: AP McDonald LLC (Applied Partners affiliate); sale to a new owner pending
status: All buildings except the office have been demolished; a sale was expected between July and October 2026, and a large data center has been proposed.
summary: Built in 1918 by U.S. Steel's Carnegie Steel subsidiary, closed by U.S. Steel in 1979–80, and reopened in 1981 as McDonald Steel, a maker of hot-rolled steel shapes. AP McDonald LLC bought the property on July 23, 2024 for $3.25 million and began demolition with asbestos and PCB removal in fall 2025. A data center has been proposed on roughly 350 acres assembled around the site.
program: Applied for a $2M Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program grant (Feb 2025) for asbestos and lead cleanup; no award reported

name: Former Niles Generating Station (Ohio Edison)
owner: Whitetail Creek LLC (Bitdeer Technologies Group subsidiary)
status: Bitdeer plans a 300 MW AI data center on the cleared site and was seeking annexation into Niles as of April 2026, amid local opposition.
summary: Ohio Edison built the coal plant in 1953; it closed in 2013 and the main structure was imploded on April 28, 2022, leaving the electrical infrastructure. Bitdeer bought the site on May 5, 2025 for $3.4 million and is targeting power delivery around 2028–2029.

name: Former Warren Steel / Copperweld Steel mill
address: Mahoning Ave. NW near the SR 82 / SR 45 interchange
formerUse: Steel mill (Copperweld Steel / CSC Ltd., later Warren Steel Holdings)
status: A court approved foreclosure in April 2026, clearing the way for a sheriff's appraisal and sale; Ohio Star Forge still operates on part of the property.
summary: Copperweld moved to Warren in 1939. Warren Steel Holdings bought the mill out of bankruptcy in 2001, and it shut down for good in 2016. Ohio EPA found abandoned chemicals, oil pits and hazardous materials in 2019, and the property is now under a court-approved environmental covenant.
program: Ohio EPA-overseen cleanup under a court-approved environmental covenant

name: Former Youngstown Sheet & Tube Campbell Works (Casey Drive Industrial Park)
formerUse: Steel mill (Youngstown Sheet & Tube Campbell Works)
status: Part of the former works is now the Casey Drive Industrial Park; a $299,856 state remediation application was filed in February 2025, with no award reported.
summary: The Casey Drive Industrial Park occupies part of Youngstown Sheet & Tube's former Campbell Works. A $299,856 site-remediation request for it was one of five Mahoning County applications in the February 2025 Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program round, when the state portal filled within about an hour. EPA's ACRES list separately includes the Youngstown Sheet & Tube Seamless Tube Mill parcel nearby in Struthers.
program: Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program application ($299,856, Feb 2025; award not reported)

name: Former Republic Steel Lorain mill
address: Lorain Works complex along the Black River, north of E. 28th St.
status: Idle and deteriorating; the city cited code violations, and in late 2025 Grupo Simec was reported in talks with international producers about a restart.
summary: Steelmaking on the site began in 1895. Republic cut the mill to about 100 workers in 2016 and stopped all operations in 2022. City inspectors in 2024 reported flooded basements, collapsing roofs and debris piles and said they would refer violations to Ohio EPA. EPA's ACRES list includes one separate parcel of the old Lorain Works (the turning basin), but not the mill.

name: Former Avon Lake Power Plant
owner: Avon Lake Environmental Redevelopment Group (Charah Solutions affiliate)
status: Remediation to Ohio EPA standards is ongoing; the site was rezoned in May 2026 and the city is buying about 23 acres for a lakefront park.
summary: The plant generated its last power in March 2022. Asbestos removal and demolition, including implosions beginning in 2024, were expected to wrap up around spring 2025, and the owner is marketing the remainder for mixed-use development.

name: Former Eastlake Power Plant
address: Lake Erie shoreline near the mouth of the Chagrin River
formerUse: Coal-fired power plant (Cleveland Electric Illuminating / FirstEnergy)
status: A 2025 state grant funds demolition of 11 vacant buildings and soil cleanup; a coal-ash refining pilot opened on the site in September 2026.
summary: Two coal units were deactivated in 2012 and the last three shut down in April 2015; synchronous condensers still operate on part of the 120-acre parcel. Industrial Development Advantage took the property and its environmental liabilities from Energy Harbor and is marketing about 65 acres for industrial, energy or data-center use.

name: Former Cleveland Thermal steam plant
formerUse: Coal-fired district steam plant (built by Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co.)
owner: Corix Cleveland Thermal Generating LP (as of June 2025; Bedrock affiliate pursuing purchase)
status: A June 2025 state grant funds remediation and demolition, with Bedrock planning mixed-use riverfront development.
summary: Opened in 1894, the plant heated more than 100 downtown buildings with coal-fired steam for over a century before closing in December 2016. The Cuyahoga Land Bank won about $2.5M toward $4.9M in demolition and cleanup costs.
program: Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program grant (~$2.5M, 2025) via Cuyahoga Land Bank

name: Former Lake Shore Power Plant (CEI / FirstEnergy)
formerUse: Coal-fired power plant (Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co. Lake Shore Power Station)
owner: Lake Shore Acquisition Company LLC (Industrial Development Advantage affiliate)
status: Remediated in 2024–25 and offered for sale or lease in February 2026 for industrial, logistics, data-center or mixed-use development; remaining structures are slated for demolition by 2028.
summary: CEI built the plant in 1911; it closed in 2015 and was imploded in 2017. Industrial Development Advantage acquired it from Energy Harbor with all environmental liabilities, and the two companies spent several million dollars on remediation. Community groups are pushing for housing and parks on the lakefront site.

name: Former Republic Steel Canton mill
status: As of August 2024 the mill was standing and deteriorating while the city negotiated a transfer to a developer for brownfield cleanup.
summary: Grupo Simec idled the Canton mill in August 2023 and closed it permanently that October, citing weak demand and high costs; about 500 workers were furloughed across its Canton and Lackawanna, N.Y. mills. Residents had long complained about lead and air emissions.

name: Former Westinghouse Electric plant (Mansfield)
formerUse: Appliance and electrical equipment manufacturing (Westinghouse Electric, 1918–1990)
status: Demolition and cleanup are complete; the cleared site awaits a redevelopment partner.
summary: Westinghouse operated the plant from 1918 until the end of 1990, employing more than 8,000 people at its peak. The Richland County Land Bank began demolition in December 2022, funded mainly by a $3M state grant, and U.S. EPA provided technical assistance with a market analysis for mixed-use redevelopment.
program: State of Ohio brownfield/demolition grant ($3M, 2022); U.S. EPA Brownfields and Land Reutilization Technical Assistance (2024)

name: Former W.C. Beckjord Power Station
formerUse: Coal-fired power plant (Cincinnati Gas & Electric / Duke Energy)
status: The plant is demolished; coal-ash remediation continues and is the subject of a federal lawsuit allowed to proceed in 2024.
summary: CG&E opened the plant in 1952 and Duke Energy retired it in 2014. In 2018 Duke transferred it to Commercial Liability Partners, which assumed coal-ash liability in exchange for about $105M in cleanup funds. Millions of tons of coal ash remain in ponds near the Ohio River.
